subject: Code runs locally, but unable to run on computing cluster

messages.author: 7e5b5ac76117f50b
messages.subject: Code runs locally, but unable to run on computing cluster
parts:
Hi all,

I have a model that functions on my personal laptop, but cannot run on a computing cluster, which I am using to speed up the model selection process. I assume this is an issue with the INLA or R version, but I am unable to update R beyond version 4.3.2 (2023-10-31), which limits INLA to between versions 24.03.29 on the HPC. I have used inla.binary.install() and selected Centos07 for the HPC. Notably, my laptop is windows and using only a slightly different version of INLA, 24.03.09. (Scared to update my laptop's INLA package now). 

Any suggestions? Do I have any options for adjusting the installed packages, model components, or inputs to get this model run on the system I have available?  

I have attached the verbose output and code, (tried attaching a data stack but google wouldn't let me). There error in question reads:

GitId: ecd21b93fe64e8bc6a8b88eb034ec1a02a43f3f0 - Fri Mar 29 15:45:28 2024 +0300
Error:12 Reason: The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
Message: Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE
Line:1043 Function: GMRFLib_init_GMRF_approximation_store__intern

Do I have any options for adjusting the model components or inputs to get this model run on the system I have available?  

The model is a joint likelihood zero-inflated poisson, where point count data ("unstr") is being supplemented by presence-only data ("po"). In the formula below, Z = Use (Zero-Inflation term, binomial), Y = Abundance (zeroinflatedpoisson0). The model includes a shared random effect for Y, a covariate to account for distance traveled during a survey, independent SPDEs for both use and abundance, and an SPDE to control for effort. I have pulled out just the formula and INLA call below for easy reading

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Code runs locally, but unable to run on computing cluster
parts:
hi,

the easy way out is the compile and install R-4.4 on the cluster yourself, and
just install it locally for you, like

./configure --prefix=$HOME/local
make

and just run your own R-4.4

would that be possible? it depends on your linux skills but its a straight
forward thing to do, so unless you're able yourself, then a geek friend might
help you out. 

[this solution is what I have done in the past in these situations]

you can use the CentOS7 build but the recent ones also contains Rocky8, which is
the 'free version'; of rhel8

parts:
Thank you for the suggestion, it took a while to implement due to permission issues. I have been able to update R and INLA within my own allocation on our HPC to ensure they are both the most up to date versions. Unfortunately, I am still receiving the same error as before. 

GitId: 6bf32bef39d6c4d87ae87a300608e809a473723a - Mon Oct 7 13:02:06 2024 +0300

Error:12 Reason: The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
Message: Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE

Line:1044 Function: GMRFLib_init_GMRF_approximation_store__intern

I have attached the new verbose output, along with a more detailed version of the Rscript showing how the INLA stacks were constructed, in case there is anything there.

Are there any other explanations for this issue that would explain it running on a standard laptop but not a computing cluster?  Could it be another r package? Or potentially another bash module that is out of date? My IT person indicated I must load these modules to ensure the script worked within R: gdal, proj, sqlite, geos, curl, gsl, fribidi, harfbuzz, freetype. Could they be conflicting in some way?

Or is it possible that its a specific Linux issue? My HPC linux install information: version is 4.18.0-513.5.1.el8_9.x86_64 (gcc version 8.5.0 20210514 (Red Hat 8.5.0-20)

Any suggestions would be helpful, thanks.
